title: ESA Hera mission to perform braking manoeuvres
excerpt: The spacecraft will ignite thrusters on October 15 to reduce its velocity relative to the Didymos asteroid system.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced on October 7, 2026, that the Hera spacecraft is preparing for a series of braking manoeuvres to approach its target asteroids. The mission, which launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on October 7, 2024, is currently travelling at a speed of more than 12 kilometres per second relative to Earth.

On October 15, Hera will rotate to align its ring of Orbit Control Thrusters to face the Didymos system. Three of these hydrazine-based thrusters will be ignited at once, burning continuously for a total of 93 minutes to reduce the spacecraft's velocity relative to the asteroids by a few hundred metres per second.

A second braking manoeuvre, known as BRM-2, is scheduled for implementation on October 22. This second thruster burn will last approximately 31 minutes and is intended to complete most of the delta-v required to match the velocity of the Didymos system, while also compensating for any performance variations during the first manoeuvre.

Following these two primary burns, the mission team will conduct three smaller transition manoeuvres toward the end of October. These final adjustments will reduce the relative velocity of the spacecraft with respect to the Didymos system down to near zero.
topic: Brake! Time for ESA’s Hera asteroid mission to go slow
